front_blocks.md: Define **packetising**.

back_blocks.md: Packetising is the process of **dividing a large message into smaller, manageable units called packets**, each of which can be transmitted individually.

cards.front_md: Define **packetising**.

front_blocks.md: Name the three parts of a packet.

back_blocks.md: **Header**, **payload** and **footer (trailer)**.

cards.front_md: Name the three parts of a packet.
cards.back_md: **Header**, **payload** and **footer (trailer)**.

front_blocks.md: Define **payload**.

back_blocks.md: The payload is the **actual data being sent**.

front_blocks.md: Name four items found in a packet header.

back_blocks.md: **Source IP address**, **destination IP address**, **sequence number**, **protocol**, **packet length** and **checksum**.

front_blocks.md: What is the sequence number in a packet header used for?

back_blocks.md: To **reassemble the packets in the correct order** at the destination.

front_blocks.md: How do packets travel across a network?

back_blocks.md: **Independently**, and they may travel along **different routes** through the network.

cards.front_md: How do packets travel across a network?
cards.back_md: **Independently**, and they may travel along **different routes** through the network.

front_blocks.md: How is the original message recovered?

front_blocks.md: Define **packet switching**.

back_blocks.md: Packet switching is a communication method where **data is broken into packets** and sent across a **shared network**, with each packet possibly taking a different path and reassembled on arrival.

cards.front_md: Define **packet switching**.
cards.back_md: Packet switching is a communication method where **data is broken into packets** and sent across a **shared network**, with each packet possibly taking a different path and reassembled on arrival.

front_blocks.md: Define **circuit switching**.

back_blocks.md: Circuit switching sets up a **dedicated communication path** between two devices for the duration of a session.

cards.front_md: Define **circuit switching**.
cards.back_md: Circuit switching sets up a **dedicated communication path** between two devices for the duration of a session.

front_blocks.md: Circuit switching works like a traditional <u>**          **</u> call.

back_blocks.md: Circuit switching works like a traditional **phone** call.

cards.front_md: Circuit switching works like a traditional <u>**          **</u> call.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Packet switching sends data as a continuous stream.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Packet switching sends data in **individual packets**. It is **circuit switching** that sends a continuous stream.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Packet switching sends data as a continuous stream.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Packet switching sends data in **individual packets**. It is **circuit switching** that sends a continuous stream.

front_blocks.md: Name three benefits of packet switching.

back_blocks.md: **Efficient use of network bandwidth**, **more reliable** because only lost or corrupted packets need resending, and **lower cost** because network resources are shared.

cards.front_md: Name three benefits of packet switching.
cards.back_md: **Efficient use of network bandwidth**, **more reliable** because only lost or corrupted packets need resending, and **lower cost** because network resources are shared.

front_blocks.md: Name three drawbacks of packet switching.

back_blocks.md: **Not ideal for real-time applications**, packets can **arrive out of order** and need reassembly, and network congestion may cause **packet delay or loss**.

cards.front_md: Name three drawbacks of packet switching.
cards.back_md: **Not ideal for real-time applications**, packets can **arrive out of order** and need reassembly, and network congestion may cause **packet delay or loss**.

front_blocks.md: Name three benefits of circuit switching.

back_blocks.md: It is ideal for **real-time communication** with a steady continuous flow, there are **no delays** once the circuit is established, and data **arrives in order**.

cards.front_md: Name three benefits of circuit switching.
cards.back_md: It is ideal for **real-time communication** with a steady continuous flow, there are **no delays** once the circuit is established, and data **arrives in order**.

front_blocks.md: Name three drawbacks of circuit switching.

back_blocks.md: It is **less efficient** because resources stay reserved when not in use, it has a **higher cost** due to dedicated lines, and it is **less scalable**.

cards.front_md: Name three drawbacks of circuit switching.
cards.back_md: It is **less efficient** because resources stay reserved when not in use, it has a **higher cost** due to dedicated lines, and it is **less scalable**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In circuit switching, resources are freed when the line is idle.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Resources **remain reserved even when not in use**, which is what makes circuit switching less efficient.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

In circuit switching, resources are freed when the line is idle.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Resources **remain reserved even when not in use**, which is what makes circuit switching less efficient.

front_blocks.md: How does data order differ between the two switching methods?

back_blocks.md: With **packet switching**, data **may arrive out of order** and requires reassembly. With **circuit switching**, data **always arrives in order**.

cards.front_md: How does data order differ between the two switching methods?
cards.back_md: With **packet switching**, data **may arrive out of order** and requires reassembly. With **circuit switching**, data **always arrives in order**.

front_blocks.md: Which switching method is more robust to failure, and why?

back_blocks.md: **Packet switching**, because packets can be **rerouted** if a failure occurs. In circuit switching, if the path fails the call is **dropped and must be re-established**.

cards.front_md: Which switching method is more robust to failure, and why?
cards.back_md: **Packet switching**, because packets can be **rerouted** if a failure occurs. In circuit switching, if the path fails the call is **dropped and must be re-established**.

front_blocks.md: Which switching method is more scalable?

back_blocks.md: **Packet switching**, which handles large volumes of data and users. Circuit switching needs **more physical paths** as more users are added.

cards.front_md: Which switching method is more scalable?
cards.back_md: **Packet switching**, which handles large volumes of data and users. Circuit switching needs **more physical paths** as more users are added.

front_blocks.md: What is packet switching best used for?

back_blocks.md: **Emails, web pages and file downloads**.

cards.front_md: What is packet switching best used for?
cards.back_md: **Emails, web pages and file downloads**.

front_blocks.md: What is circuit switching best used for?

back_blocks.md: **Real-time communication**, such as voice calls and video conferencing.

cards.front_md: What is circuit switching best used for?
cards.back_md: **Real-time communication**, such as voice calls and video conferencing.
